notes: A Security op with a real middle: sign up, go out to a Bastok-held area, hand each of the construction NPCs the right crystal, ride the Arbiter back, report. The Arbiter carries no zone -- the page says only "any Bastok controlled area" and which areas Bastok holds rotates with front-line control, so a recorded zone would be a marker in a place the player may not be able to use. Bullet [2] IS a step even though nothing is carried and nobody is named: the crystal orders are the operation. The page describes the recipients only by race and dress ("Young Elvaan wearing a red hat"), so the target stays none. The whole "After the walkthrough: Notes" section is one bullet holding the crystal-to-NPC key -- reference data a player reads, not rungs. Campaign Rank "Allied Ribbon of Glory §§§§" is the only requirement the header states and there is no schema field for a campaign rank; gates.level means CHARACTER level and would be a lie, so the rank lives here and in a flag. Repeatable is null, not true: campaign ops are repeatable in general but this page never says so. The Campaign Header template has no Expansion field, so gates.expansion is null although this is Wings of the Goddess content.

notes:
Twelve bullets, six of them steps. [5] (Sneak Attack from behind), [6] (avoiding Guard aggro), [10] (you need not see the Quartermaster first) and [12] (respawn timer) are tactics, advice and timing -- not things the ladder should stop on. [4]'s three sub-blocks are fifteen candidate ZONES, not steps.

The kill target is the Transporter alone: bullet [7] says the two Guards warp away once it dies, so they are not recorded as mobs. The page names the Transporter three ways -- Quadav, Orcish, Yagudo -- one per beastman type, and which one you meet depends on which controlled zone you pick. All three are recorded so that whichever is actually in front of you can be marked; the honest cost is that the summed kill requirement reads 3 when you only ever have to kill ONE, which is why count_unobservable is flagged. No zone on the fight: any beastman-held zone qualifies and the page says outright it need not even be one in your nation's area.

The Quartermaster's zone is not spelled out in prose but the walkthrough links him as [[Quartermaster - Bastok Markets (S)|Quartermaster]]; the in-game name is "Quartermaster" and the wiki NPC page confirms Bastok Markets (S) (H-9). The [KI] Beastman Confederate crate comes from the ??? at bullet [8], is obtained AT that step, and is the only observable thing in this op -- so it is step 4's evidence and step 5's carried item, never evidence twice. Bullet [10] means step 2 is not strictly before step 4; the page's own order is kept and the exception is flagged rather than restructured. Campaign Rank "Golden Star §§§§" has no schema field and is not a character level. Repeatable null, expansion null (no Expansion field on the Campaign Header).

notes:
An escort-and-heal op with no fighting in it at all, and the page argues with itself about what it is. Campaign Type says "Military training" and the Orders line says you will "head over to the training grounds and teach a nugget what side to the axe to hold" -- neither has anything to do with the walkthrough or the Description, which are both about tending wounded evacuated to Ruhotz Silvermines. The walkthrough is detailed and internally consistent, so it is what the ladder is read from; the mismatch is recorded and flagged, and it is why this is medium rather than high.

The entry object's grid is not in the walkthrough -- that only says "follow the wall to the west". (K-8) is the header Description's own figure (which misspells the zone "North Gustaburg") and BG Wiki's [[Allied Ensign]] NPC page independently lists North Gustaberg (S) K-8, so the two agree and the rung is pinned.

Bullet [5] is the Woundpatchers' MENU TREE, printed for reference, and bullet [6]'s sub-bullets are handling advice: status ailments, MP, morale, the green name. None are rungs. They are folded into the Woundpatcher rung together with bullet [4], because it is all one continuous interaction with the same pair of NPCs -- recruit them, lead them north, then keep issuing "Commence healing, stat!" beside each casualty. The eight wounded soldiers are never named, so they cannot be the target; six of them must be cured and nothing observable counts that.

The op ENDS at the Dawn Aureola. There is no report-back to Hieronymus anywhere on this page, unlike every other Bastok op in this batch, and none is invented -- bullet [7] says you must be close to the Aureola to receive the XP that finishes it. A party of three or greater is required (bullet [2]'s sub-bullet), which has no schema field. Campaign Rank "Brass Ribbon of Service §§" is not a character level so gates.level stays null; header Time is a 30 minute in-instance limit. Repeatable null (unstated), expansion null (no Expansion field on the Campaign Header).

six cures end the objective; return to the Aureola and stay close to it or the XP is not paid. This is where the op ends -- the page has no report-back to Hieronymus and none is invented.
